title: Caramelly Brioche Bread Pudding
description: Soft custardy brioche with a warm brown-sugar and heavy-cream caramel sauce.

ingredients.item: brioche bread, torn into bite-size pieces

substitutions: Challah or soft white bread can replace brioche.
Half-and-half can replace heavy cream for a lighter sauce.

steps.text: Heat oven to 350°F and butter an 8x8-inch baking dish.
Put the torn brioche in the dish.
Whisk eggs, milk, granulated sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt.
Pour the custard evenly over the bread and gently press so the bread absorbs it.
Bake until the center is set and the top is golden, about 35–40 minutes.
Meanwhile melt 2 tablespoons butter in a small saucepan, stir in brown sugar, then heavy cream. Simmer gently until smooth and glossy.
Spoon warm caramel sauce over warm bread pudding and serve.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter an 8×8-inch baking dish with {{butter}} of the butter.
Put {{bread}} brioche, torn into bite-size pieces, into the buttered dish.
In a large bowl, whisk {{eggs}} eggs with {{milk}} milk, {{sugar}} granulated sugar, {{vanilla}} vanilla, {{cinnamon}} cinnamon, and {{salt}} salt.
Pour the custard over the bread. Gently press the bread down so it can soak up the liquid.
Bake at 350°F for 35–40 minutes, until the center looks set and the top is golden. Start with 35 minutes, then check it.
While it bakes, melt the remaining butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
As soon as the butter is melted, stir in {{brown}} packed brown sugar. Keep stirring so it melts without scorching.
Pour in {{cream}} heavy cream and stir until the sauce is smooth and glossy. Let it bubble very gently for 1–2 minutes, then take it off the heat.
Spoon warm caramel sauce over the warm bread pudding. Serve it while it is soft and custardy.

storage: Refrigerate covered up to 3 days. Reheat individual portions gently; keep extra sauce refrigerated separately if possible.

title: Easy Egg Fried Rice
description: Fast, fluffy egg fried rice built for leftover rice and flexible add-ins.
substitutions: Skip the ham for vegetarian fried rice.
Use mushrooms, cabbage, peas, carrots, or any quick-cooking leftover vegetables.
A squeeze of lime at the end is excellent.

steps.text: Scramble eggs until just set; remove to a plate.
Add oil and any vegetables or ham; cook briefly.
Add cold rice and break up clumps.
Stir in soy sauce and pepper.
Fold the eggs back in and heat through.

cookSteps.text: Crack {{eggs}} eggs into a bowl and beat them with a fork.
Heat the skillet over medium-high. Scramble the eggs until fluffy and just set, then move them to a plate.
Add {{oil}} oil to the skillet. Add the ham and/or cabbage if using, and cook until hot and just tender.
Add {{rice}} cold cooked rice. Break up the clumps and stir until the rice is hot.
Drizzle in {{soy}} soy sauce and add {{pepper}} black pepper. Stir well.
Break up the cooked eggs and fold them back into the rice. Heat for about 1 minute, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate promptly and use within 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: Lemon Pepper Tilapia with Rice
description: Simple seasoned tilapia with rice and lemon; mild, fast, and weeknight-friendly.
substitutions: Use microwave rice to cut total time further.

steps.text: Cook tilapia in butter 3–4 minutes per side until opaque and flakes easily.

cookSteps.text: Start {{rice}} rice with {{water}} water according to the package directions.
Pat {{fish}} tilapia fillets dry and season both sides with {{seasoning}} lemon pepper.
Melt {{butter}} butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the tilapia about 3–4 minutes on the first side, until the edges turn opaque.
Flip and cook another 2–4 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Serve the fish with the rice. Squeeze lemon over the top if you have it.

storage: Refrigerate cooked fish up to 2 days. Reheat gently to avoid drying it out.

title: Turkey Cheeseburger Macaroni
description: One-pan creamy ground turkey macaroni with familiar cheeseburger flavor.
substitutions: Monterey Jack or a cheddar blend can replace cheddar.

steps.text: Add macaroni, liquid, and seasonings; simmer until pasta is tender.
Stir in milk and cheese until creamy.

cookSteps.text: Put {{turkey}} ground turkey in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Break it up and cook until no pink remains.
Stir in {{pasta}} macaroni, {{water}} water or broth, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Bring it to a gentle boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered until the pasta is tender, about 12–14 minutes. Stir a few times so it does not stick.
Turn the heat low. Stir in {{milk}} milk and {{cheese}} shredded cheddar until creamy and melted.
Taste, add a pinch more salt or pepper if needed, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Add a splash of milk when reheating.
